title: Spherical gas-fueled cool diffusion flames
summary: The CFI-G results paper: 280 hot flames of ethane, propane and n-butane (normal and inverse, 0.46-3.04 bar), 189 radiatively extinguished; 15 spherical cool diffusion flames, only for 30% n-butane at 0.75-1.5 mg/s into 0.39 O2 at 2 bar with burner above 515 K; hot/cool radius ratio 2.6; a Spalding-type model with one fitted rhoD reproduces hot and cool flame radii.

items.claim: First gas-fuelled spherical cool diffusion flames, 15 in all, after radiative extinction.
items.quote: Spherical cool diffusion flames burning gases were observed for the first time. Fifteen such flames were observed.

items.claim: Narrow cool-flame window (normal n-butane, 2 bar, 0.75-1.5 mg/s, burner > 515 K).
items.quote: They were only observed for normal n-butane flames at 2 bar, and only for butane flow rates of 0.75 – 1.5 mg/s. In addition, these cool flames were only observed for burner temperatures above 515 K.

items.claim: Hot/cool radius ratio 2.6 (model 3.2), cool flame at Z = 0.53.
items.quote: The mean measured r hf / r cf is 2.6 and the mean predicted by Eq. (12) is 3.2.

items.claim: With peak temperatures assumed at 1400 K (hot) and 750 K (cool), one value rhoD = 0.0334 g/m-s (at 300 K) fitted all hot and cool flame radii (cool flames of Table 2 and quasi-steady normal n-butane hot flames at X_O2 0.37-0.40, 0.5-2 bar), with R^2 = 0.92 against measured radii.
items.quote: ρD was optimized to a value of 0.0334 g/m-s at 300 K
The data has a coefficient of determination of R2 = 0.92 with respect to the line shown with unity slope.

items.claim: Normal propane flames above 1 bar were limited to X_O2 = 0.21 (a safety constraint on the matrix).
items.quote: For propane normal flames at pressures above 1 bar, X O2 was limited to 0.21.

items.claim: Per-fuel outcome counts in Table 1 (radiatively extinguished RE / flow-terminated FT): normal ethane 30/10, propane 34/6, n-butane 46/17; inverse ethane 25/22, propane 24/13, n-butane 30/23. The PSI tables (tests.csv) give normal n-butane 38 SE / 15 FT and inverse ethane 27 SE / 22 FT; the other four groups match. The n-butane difference is consistent with the multi-flame hot-cool-hot tests (21291 A1, C1) counted as several hot flames in the paper; the inverse-ethane difference (2 more SE rows in PSI) is unexplained.

title: Cool diffusion flames in a stably stratified stagnation flow
summary: Normal-gravity laboratory method for cool diffusion flames over an n-heptane pool between heated parallel plates (stably stratified stagnation flow): peak 705-760 K, autoignition at 550 K. No ISS data.

items.claim: Ground n-heptane pool cool flames, not CFI-G gaseous ISS flames.
items.quote: A method is presented here for observing cool diffusion flames inexpensively using a pool of liquid n-heptane and parallel plates heated so as to produce a stably stratified stagnation flow.

notes: NSF PAR copy (10426594). The record gap already says this paper has no ISS data.
